llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims, but it includes under-disclosed extra data flows and developer utilities that deserve review before installation.

dimensions.detail: AISA_API_KEY and optional GitHub tokens are purpose-aligned, but queries and selected scraped content are sent to external AISA/GitHub/Reddit/YouTube/Polymarket paths, and an optional Xiaohongshu path can use a local authenticated service that is not clearly declared in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, scheduled task, service, remote payload execution, or tool replacement was found. The package ships Python and shell scripts plus a requests dependency.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md trigger and commands are broad but related to recent research; I found no artifact-backed system-prompt override or agent hijacking instruction. The main scope issue is disclosure, not deceptive instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can write persistent local state: ~/.config/last30days/.env, .last30days-data SQLite databases, home-directory briefing archives, watchlist settings, and configured webhook destinations. It does not install system persistence or modify privileged files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main pipeline coherently aggregates recent research across social, web, GitHub, and market sources, but the package also includes less-disclosed capabilities: Xiaohongshu access through a local logged-in service, arbitrary webhook notifications, watchlist/briefing storage, evaluation scripts that run git worktrees, and humor/virality scoring.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with research topics and selected result text leaving your machine for AISA and other source APIs. Do not configure webhook delivery unless you trust the destination, avoid the Xiaohongshu source unless you intend to use a local logged-in service, and do not run the evaluation scripts against untrusted git revisions while API keys are present.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Most per-file description mismatch findings are downgraded because helper modules do not need to individually implement the whole skill; the inspected pipeline does implement the advertised aggregation, planning, reranking, clustering, and JSON output.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted for extra or under-disclosed package behavior: Xiaohongshu, watchlist persistence, webhook delivery, git-worktree evaluation utilities, and fun/virality scoring are not clearly covered by the primary SKILL.md description.
[SQP-2] expected: External requests are inherent to this research skill, but disclosure should be stronger because user topics, derived queries, and candidate text can be sent to AISA and other services.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The watchlist can POST update metadata to any configured HTTPS webhook, and evaluation scripts can pass AISA_API_KEY into subprocesses running checked-out revisions; both are user-configurable but higher risk than ordinary one-shot research.
[AST4] expected: Subprocess usage is mostly fixed-argument local wrappers and Python version checks, but the evaluation helper's git worktree execution should only be used with trusted revisions.
[PE3] expected: Credential-file access appears limited to the skill's own config files and declared AISA/GitHub environment variables, not broad credential harvesting.
[PE2] unexpected: The reported privilege-escalation signal is a printed chmod recommendation for securing the skill's .env file, not execution of sudo or root commands.
[E1] expected: Outbound API calls to AISA, GitHub, Reddit, YouTube, Hacker News, and Polymarket are expected for the skill's purpose; the arbitrary configured webhook is the part that needs review.
